title: Two minutes and fifty-four seconds
note: TIMES EST FROM NTSB AAR-04/04 AND THE COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER TRANSCRIPT (NTSB DOCKET) · RADIO AND COCKPIT LINES ARE TRANSCRIPT TEXT, NOT AUDIO

events.text: The captain: "you have the airplane." The first officer will fly this leg.
Kennedy tower clears AA587 heavy for takeoff on runway 31L.
AA587 begins its takeoff roll behind the Japan Airlines B747-400 (JAL47).
Liftoff, about 1 min 40 s behind JAL47. The rule: two minutes OR four nautical miles. Actual spacing: at least 4.3 nm and 3,800 ft.
"thirteen hundred feet, we're climbing to five thousand." New York departure clears the climb to 13,000 ft.
Climbing through about 1,700 ft. Seven control-wheel movements; the rudder pedals barely move.
"we'll turn direct WAVEY." The last words air traffic control receives from AA587.
About 2,430 ft above the ground. Control wheel to 64° right at 09:15:51.5; right rudder pedal 1.7 in at 09:15:51.9.
"max power." Spoken in a strained voice, the transcript notes. Airspeed 240 kt. The pedals go 1.7R, 1.7L, 1.7R, 2.0R, 2.4L, 1.3R.
The right rear main attachment fitting fractures at 09:15:58.4 — rudder 10–11° right, sideslip 11–12°. A loud bang on the recorder at 09:15:58.5. About 251 kt.
Last synchronized flight-data point, 13.6 s before impact. Sideslip has reached 31°.
"what the hell are we into. we're stuck in it."
"get out of it, get out of it."
The cockpit voice recorder stops when electrical power is lost, 30 min 39 s after it began.
Newport Avenue and Beach 131st Street, Belle Harbor. 260 aboard and five on the ground are killed: 265.
